title: Ample pullback by an immersion with quasi-compact source
statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $i:Y\to X$ be an immersion (a closed immersion into an open subscheme of $X$, followed by its inclusion) [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion], and assume $Y$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. If $L$ is an ample invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], then its tensor pullback $i^*L$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is an ample invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module. No Noetherian, finite-type or separatedness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: By the definition of ampleness, $X$ is quasi-compact. Apply [lem-sfb-ample-nonvanishing-basis-criterion] to $L$: the opens $X_s$, with $s\in\Gamma(X,L^{\otimes n})$ and $n\geq1$, form a basis of $X$.

source.place: Tag 0B3E, lemma-ample-on-locally-closed, proof, application of proposition-characterize-ample (01Q3) on X.

proof.text: Put $M=i^*L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](1),(2), $M$ is invertible and, iterating the tensor comparison, $i^*(L^{\otimes n})\cong M^{\otimes n}$. For a section $s$ as above let $t=i^*s$ under this comparison. Clause (3), applied to the invertible module $L^{\otimes n}$, gives $t(y)=s(i(y))\otimes1$ over $\kappa(i(y))\to\kappa(y)$. A vector in the one-dimensional fibre stays nonzero after field extension: choose a basis and its coefficient is carried by an injective field map. Hence $Y_t=i^{-1}(X_s)$.

source.place: Tag 0B3E, proof, tensor-power pullback and equality of nonvanishing loci; Modules Remark 0H78 (remark-pullback-s-open).

proof.text: Factor $i$ as a closed immersion $c:Y\to U$ and an open immersion $j:U\to X$. Their definitions identify $Y$ with a subspace of $U$ and $U$ with an open subspace of $X$. Thus every open $V\subseteq Y$ has the form $i^{-1}(W)$ for an open $W\subseteq X$: write $V=c^{-1}(A)$ for $A$ open in $U$, then write $A=j^{-1}(W)$. If $y\in V$, step 1 gives $i(y)\in X_s\subseteq W$. Step 2 gives $y\in Y_{i^*s}=i^{-1}(X_s)\subseteq V$. Therefore the pulled-back positive-power sections already give a basis; allowing all sections of powers of $M$ still gives a basis.

source.place: Tag 0B3E, proof, reduction from (2) to (4) and the subspace-topology argument.

proof.text: The scheme $Y$ is quasi-compact by hypothesis and $M$ is invertible by step 2. Step 3 verifies the basis condition for $M$, so [lem-sfb-ample-nonvanishing-basis-criterion] implies that $M=i^*L$ is ample. This proves both invertibility and ampleness.

source.place: Tag 0B3E, proof, final application of proposition-characterize-ample (01Q3) on X′.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0B3E, lemma-ample-on-locally-closed, proof of (4), specialized to condition (2).

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q02-216b81905 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item, the one new node, every cited statement, and Stacks properties.tex:4557 (01Q3), properties.tex:4759 (0B3E) and modules.tex:4404 (0H78). The 4 steps follow the 0B3E proof of (4), specialized to (2). Step 1: the ampleness definition (01PS) gives X quasi-compact, and the new criterion (01Q3 (1)=>(3)) gives a basis of nonvanishing loci X_s. Step 2: the Lean-closed lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor gives M=i^*L invertible (clause 1), the iso i^*(L^n)=M^n (clause 2) and the fibre value (i^*s)(y)=s(i(y))⊗1 (clause 3). The field-extension nonvanishing argument is written out, so Y_t equals i^{-1}(X_s) exactly. Step 3 is an elementary subspace-topology argument from the closed and open immersion definitions and assumes no affine preimages (A^2 minus 0 in A^2 is the reason). Step 4 applies 01Q3 (3)=>(1) on Y, which is quasi-compact by hypothesis. New node lem-sfb-ample-nonvanishing-basis-criterion matches 01Q3 (1)<=>(3) hypothesis by hypothesis (X quasi-compact, n>=1, no affine, Noetherian or separatedness assumption). It is statement-only and self-contained. I tested it on empty X and on Spec A with O_X; an infinite discrete union of points shows the quasi-compact hypothesis is needed. It is not a restated clause of the item.
